abstract.title: TWELVE-MONTH INHALATION STUDY ON ROOM-AGED CIGARETTE SIDESTREAM SMOKE (RASS) IN RATS

study_details.exposure: Whole-body exposed to RASS, an environmental tobacco smoke surrogate, at 6 and 12 µg total particulate matter/l for 12 h/d, 5 d/week, 12 months
study_details.comparison: Another group of rats was head-only exposed at 12 µg/l for 7 h/d

findings.nicotine_concentration: Reducing the concentrations of nicotine, formaldehyde, and catechol
findings.urinary_analysis: Additional uptake by routes other than inhalation as shown by analysis of the urinary nicotine metabolites
findings.inflammation: No sign of pulmonary inflammation was seen (differential counting of bronchoalveolar lavage cells)
findings.dna_damage: Slight increase in oxidative DNA damage (8-hydroxy-deoxyguanosine) in the nasal respiratory epithelium but not in total pulmonary DNA
findings.histopathological_changes: Minimal to moderate reserve cell hyperplasia and squamous metaplasia as well as minimal olfactory epithelium atrophy; slight eosinophilic globules in sustentacular cells of the olfactory epithelium; pronounced squamous metaplasia and hyperplasia in the larynx at the base of epiglottis; and slight reserve cell hyperplasia in the bronchi. The hyper- and metaplastic changes are considered adaptive and were similar to those seen in subchronic sidestream smoke inhalation studies in rats.
